title: precheck names each committed item's goal clauses with the check that reads each, and warns of a clause no check reads
goal: Answers the SP-s5fdczv7 retrospective: all three code items (BG-m6fknqr5, BG-tyuwiin7, ST-dets7lkp) carried a check that read one clause of a several-clause goal (a source-order read, one command mapping, one cost header line), so the other clauses were proved only by the orchestrator and the reviewer, and BG-ese7wmz3 and BG-47kw57ed got through. backlog.py precheck SP prints, for each committed item, its goal's clauses (split as close --summary splits a sprint goal) and the check or repro that reads each, from a mapping the planner records on the item, and warns of a clause no check reads, so kb-sprint plan step 6 is a tool output, not a reading; kb-sprint plan step 6, backlog.md and tools.md say so.

gates.question: Where does the planner record which check reads each goal clause, so precheck can warn of an unread one?
options: a clauses field on the item: a list of {clause, check} pairs, the check an index into checks or repro, validated by backlog.py check
a notes line per clause (Clause: <text> -> check <n>), parsed by precheck, no schema change
gates.recommendation: a clauses field on the item: a list of {clause, check} pairs, the check an index into checks or repro, validated by backlog.py check

notes: Its check is a placeholder that passes before the work: once gate g1 is answered, sprint planning replaces it with a planted item whose clause no check reads, which precheck must warn of.
